olivia (acme-poc): Hey team — during our demo this morning we started seeing a bunch of 5xxs (~10% of requests) around 09:12 PDT. Customers are hitting simple text-complete endpoints. Can someone triage?

ravi (sales): Thanks for flagging, @olivia. We're on the call in 10m. Any logs or request IDs you can paste here?

olivia (acme-poc): Pasting a sample of the response headers and body we received:

```
HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2026 16:12:34 GMT
x-rd-error: capacity_throttle
x-request-id: req_0a7f8b2c
Content-Type: application/json
\n{"error":"upstream unavailable","code":503}
```

elaine (support): Seeing `capacity_throttle` header means the serving layer returned a soft throttle. Can you share the workload pattern? bursty or steady?

olivia (acme-poc): It's a short burst from a demo harness — 120 rps for ~30s, then back to baseline. We expected Dedicated POC to absorb that.

mike (eng-runtime): Hmm. That burst should be handled by burstpool. I'm checking autoscale and node events now. @joel can you correlate cluster metrics with these request IDs?

\

joel (eng-sre): Looking at the metrics around 16:12: CPU on the pool spiked, queue depth rose, and we hit the configured concurrency limit for that model variant. Autoscaler started but there was a ~18s delay before new workers registered. That's the window where requests were 503'ing.

elaine (support): Two probable issues: (1) burstpool capacity ephemeral exhaustion, (2) autoscale cold start latency. We should confirm if fallback routing to lower-capacity variant occurred.

mike (eng-runtime): Running a quick grep on the logs for req_0a7f8b2c — found this on the runtime host:

```
[16:12:33.987] WARN  runtime::throttle - capacity_throttle triggered, queue_len=42, live_workers=6, max_workers=6
[16:12:34.002] ERROR runtime::scheduler - reject request req_0a7f8b2c: no available slot
[16:12:34.010] INFO  runtime::autoscale - scale_event: desired=9, current=6, reason="queue_growth"
```

ravi (sales): Customer asking why fallback to a smaller model wasn't used. They want consistent availability even during demo spikes.

mike (eng-runtime): We have two options: enable immediate fallback routing to a cheaper compatible variant (sacrifices latency/quality but keeps availability), or increase burstpool headroom & pre-warm additional workers for POC customers.

elaine (support): I checked the POC config — fallback routing was OFF by default for this account. We can flip it per-tenant. Also the burstpool for this Dedicated instance is set to +2 workers. For 120 rps burst that's insufficient.

olivia (acme-poc): If we enable fallback, will the API return 200s with a different model id or a special header? We need to be transparent to the demo attendees.

mike (eng-runtime): Fallback will route to variant `gptx-lite-v1` and the response will include `x-rd-fallback: true` and `x-model-variant: gptx-lite-v1`. Body still 200 unless the downstream variant errors.

joel (eng-sre): Quick mitigation I applied: increased burstpool headroom to +6 and reduced autoscale cooldown to 8s for this pool. Should reduce future 5xx window. Watch the dashboards: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/poc-12345/overview (linking metrics for the pool).

olivia (acme-poc): I see the recent calls now mostly 200s. Thanks. Any durable fix recommended before our follow-up demo at 11:00?

elaine (support): Recommended durable changes for POC: 1) enable fallback routing for demo routes; 2) bump burstpool to +4 for demo windows; 3) add a lightweight pre-warm policy for expected demo times. I can submit the config change if you approve.

ravi (sales): Please do the config change, @elaine. Also add an entry in the POC runbook so customer engineers know fallback semantics. Olivia — sending a short note to the customer that we've enabled fallback and increased burstpool, and that we'll monitor.

mike (eng-runtime): Follow-up action for eng-runtime: investigate why autoscaler take ~18s to register new workers during this workload. Possibly image pull / cold JIT compilation on the models. I'll open ENG-RUNTIME ticket with logs.

joel (eng-sre): FYI I also left a note on the cluster that we hit ephemeral quota for this pool during the demo — might want to request a temporary quota bump from infra.

olivia (acme-poc): Great — appreciate the quick turnaround. We'll confirm behavior in the 11:00 run. Will report back if we still see 5xx.

deploy-bot: deploy v2026.3.21-428 applied to pool poc-12345 by joel — scaling policy adjusted

elaine (support): Closing the immediate ticket; will follow up with a summary and the runbook snippet. :thumbsup:
